subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discovery — MedSys (post-call notes)
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discovery — MedSys (post-call notes)

Alicia — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned. Notes below are high-level; I'm attaching a preliminary reserved-GPU estimate and a short ops runbook sketch.

Summary of pain & goals
- Production latency variability across peak windows (95th pctl spikes to ~1.8s) is causing metric regressions for your real-time clinical triage service.
- Current cloud setup faces noisy-neighbor interference during morning batch runs; isolation is a priority for you.
- Goal: predictable 99th pctl latency under 1.1s and throughput to support 120 qps sustained with 300 qps burst for scheduled windows.

Constraints discussed
- Strict PHI segmentation; you need VPC isolation and customer-managed keys for audit trails.
- Procurement timeline target: sign-off within 6–8 weeks; budget band mentioned ~USD 130k/year for reserved capacity.

Proposed configuration (initial)
- Dedicated pool: 8x A100s (reserved) with two isolated lanes (prod / batch).
- Isolation level: tenant-level vGPU isolation + dedicated inference pool (no multi-tenant inference on these nodes).
- SLA targets we can commit to (subject to contract): 99.5% uptime, 99th pctl latency target 1.1s for primary model; fallback routing to lower-cost variant if a node becomes unhealthy.
- Autoscale & burst: scheduled burst capacity to add 4 GPUs for 2-hour windows, with warm standby to hit burst SLOs.

Next steps (owner tags)
- Nikhil: send detailed reserved-GPU cost worksheet + ops MOP (attached) — by EOD tomorrow.
- Alicia: introduce procurement contact and share any specific security evidence pack asks (SOC-2, encryption attestation) — by EOW.
- Ben: prepare a short tech-runbook for on-call and fallbacks that maps to MedSys runbook expectations.

Attachments
- redwood_reserved_gpu_estimate.xlsx (cost worksheet)
- medsys_sample-mop.pdf (ops checklist stub)

If that all aligns, I'll scope a formal proposal and an initial SOW draft next week. Thanks again — appreciate the clear priorities.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

Thanks, Nikhil — that aligns well with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our end:

- The 120 qps sustained target is for inference events triggered by our triage pipeline (peak windows are usually 07:00–09:30 local). The burst up to 300 qps would be scheduled at those windows for 45–90 minutes at a time.
- For PHI concerns, our security team will require evidence for data-at-rest encryption, KMS integration details, and an audit log export cadence (daily/weekly).
- Procurement (cc'ed) — we are aiming to review pricing and SLA language within the next three weeks; please send the cost breakdown and any standard commercial terms you expect.

Procurement contact: Maria Chen (maria.chen@medsys.ai) — Maria, Nikhil from Redwood has the initial sizing and ops sketch attached. Can you advise on the legal procurement cadence and any additional documents you need?

Appreciate the clear owners — Alicia

Maria — great to meet you by intro. Per Alicia's ask, attaching the cost worksheet and a concise evidence checklist we typically provide for SOC2/KMS/audit logs. High-level clarifications below: 

SLA & runbook highlights (proposal baseline)
- Latency SLA: 99th pctl <= 1.1s for the primary model at 120 qps sustained.
- Uptime SLA: 99.5% monthly uptime for dedicated pool.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to a quantized-compatible variant if latency degrades >30% over 5m window; we also provide a warm-standby burst lane that brings additional GPUs to warm state within 90s.
- Audit logs: daily export to your S3 bucket (encrypted in transit and at rest), retention configurable up to 1 year (we can extend subject to contract).

Ops & security pack (attached)
- SOC 2 Type II report stub, KMS integration notes, sample audit log schema, and our recommended MOP for canary/rollouts.

Questions to close the proposal
1) Will MedSys accept a 12-month reserved commitment with a 30-day termination clause for regulatory reasons?
2) Any minimum acceptable SLA changes? If you need 99.9% uptime we will need an uplift in pricing and a multi-region standby.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0: finalize sizing and commercial terms (this week–three weeks).
- Week 1–2: legal + SOC addendum review.
- Week 3–4: onboarding kickoff and environment provision (dry-run canary within 10 business days after kickoff).

I'm happy to set up a short call with our Security & Solutions Engineering leads (cc Marissa) if that helps accelerate the evidence review.

Best,
Nikhil
